title: Google Clips
summary:
Google Clips is a discontinued miniature clip-on camera device developed by Google. It was announced on October 4, 2017 and went on sale on January 27, 2018. Google Clips automatically captured video clips (without audio) at moments its machine learning algorithms determined to be interesting or relevant.

The camera had 16 GB of built-in storage, could record clips for up to 3 hours, shot still photos at 15 frames per second to create segments, and featured a 12 megapixel sensor. It was originally priced at US$249. An indicator flashed when the camera was looking for scenes to capture. The AI could learn the faces of people to take photographs with certain people, and could automatically set lighting and framing.

All machine learning happened on the device itself, so nothing left the device until the user decided to save and share it. It had no microphone, so it could not record sound. To train Clips in photography, Google hired a documentary photographer, a photojournalist, and a fine arts photographer using a strategy called human-centered machine learning. The AI was trained on composition (stability, sharpness, and framing), recognizing social norms, and editing (picking out special photos instead of mundane ones).

Google Clips was withdrawn from sale on October 15, 2019, but supported until the end of December 2021.
